newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt not in talks on Nordbanken - official.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt not in talks on Nordbanken - official.

text.p: The Swedish government is not in any negotiations over its stake in Nordbanken, a finance ministry spokeswoman said on Friday on behalf of Finance Minister Erik Asbrink.
"The state is not taking part in any negotiations concerning Nordbanken," said Asbrink's spokeswoman Anna Forsberg.
"As for the rest, he (Asbrink) has no comment on rumours that circulate."

Business newspaper Dagens Industri on Friday reported that the government had talks over the holiday period and was expected to sell 20-25 percent of the state's slice of Nordbanken to Investor AB, the investment arm of the Wallenberg industrial empire.

Swedish banking shares jumped early Friday on the report. Nordbanken jumped 14.5 crowns at the opening to 230 crowns after rising nine crowns on Thursday amid merger rumours. The bank sector index rose 1.98 percent against a rise on the market overall of 0.62 percent. Investor shares rose two crowns to 297 crowns.

Dagens Industri said the prospective sale would pave the way for a merger between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken of which the Wallenberg family owns 15 percent of capital and 16 percent of votes, the paper said.
The newspaper said negotiations about a merger between the banks are expected to start during the second part of February or the beginning of March.
But if the government has not been in any talks over the state's holding in Nordbanken, then the proposed deal reported by Dagens Industri would appear to be without foundation.
Investor has declined to comment saying out of principle it makes no comment on market rumours and speculation.
